"executive_summary": "Open-shell organic radicals are usually unstable in air because of unsatisfied valency, which has limited their use as photothermal materials. This work introduces aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs), a class of neutral conjugated nitrogen oxide radicals that are stabilized by rich resonance structures combining closed-shell nitro-like and open-shell nitroxide forms with unpaired electrons delocalized over conjugated backbones. The authors prepared a series of star-shaped ANARs by demethylating phenolic hydroxyl precursors and oxidizing them in air, without using steric hindrance protecting groups. The resulting materials show extremely high spin concentration and strongly enhanced nonradiative decay, which is exactly what is needed for efficient photothermal conversion. Among the four compounds (TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8), TPA-TPA-O6 stands out with the highest photothermal conversion performance and negligible photobleaching. The material also showed excellent photothermal stability over ten on/off laser cycles and promising seawater desalination behavior. summary.title: Stable open-shell aromatic nitric acid radicals: accessing highly efficient photothermal conversion with restricted radiative decay
summary.authors: Zejun Wang; Jiawen Zhou; Yiheng Zhang; Weiya Zhu; Yuan Li
summary.executive_summary: Open-shell organic radicals are usually unstable in air because of unsatisfied valency, which has limited their use as photothermal materials. This work introduces aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs), a class of neutral conjugated nitrogen oxide radicals that are stabilized by rich resonance structures combining closed-shell nitro-like and open-shell nitroxide forms with unpaired electrons delocalized over conjugated backbones. The authors prepared a series of star-shaped ANARs by demethylating phenolic hydroxyl precursors and oxidizing them in air, without using steric hindrance protecting groups. The resulting materials show extremely high spin concentration and strongly enhanced nonradiative decay, which is exactly what is needed for efficient photothermal conversion. Among the four compounds (TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8), TPA-TPA-O6 stands out with the highest photothermal conversion performance and negligible photobleaching. When used in an interfacial solar-driven water evaporation system built on polyurethane foam, TPA-TPA-O6 achieved a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 89.41% and a water evaporation rate of 1.293 kg m^-2 h^-1 under one sun, representing top performance among pure organic small-molecule photothermal materials. The material also showed excellent photothermal stability over ten on/off laser cycles and promising seawater desalination behavior. The study provides a low-cost, two-step synthesis strategy and a new design concept for stable high-spin radical photothermal materials.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
Open-shell organic radicals are usually unstable in air because of unsatisfied valency, which has limited their use as photothermal materials. This work introduces aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs), a class of neutral conjugated nitrogen oxide radicals that are stabilized by rich resonance structures combining closed-shell nitro-like and open-shell nitroxide forms with unpaired electrons delocalized over conjugated backbones. The authors prepared a series of star-shaped ANARs by demethylating phenolic hydroxyl precursors and oxidizing them in air, without using steric hindrance protecting groups. The resulting materials show extremely high spin concentration and strongly enhanced nonradiative decay, which is exactly what is needed for efficient photothermal conversion. Among the four compounds (TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8), TPA-TPA-O6 stands out with the highest photothermal conversion performance and negligible photobleaching. When used in an interfacial solar-driven water evaporation system built on polyurethane foam, TPA-TPA-O6 achieved a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 89.41% and a water evaporation rate of 1.293 kg m^-2 h^-1 under one sun, representing top performance among pure organic small-molecule photothermal materials. The material also showed excellent photothermal stability over ten on/off laser cycles and promising seawater desalination behavior. The study provides a low-cost, two-step synthesis strategy and a new design concept for stable high-spin radical photothermal materials.

Research Context
Open-shell organic radicals are widely studied for their unique chemical and physical properties. These radicals have potential applications in optoelectronics, organic magnets, photothermal, thermoelectric and spintronic materials. Narrow optical band gaps can be achieved through reasonable chemical modification and structural control. Radical materials have good biocompatibility, attracting attention for photothermal conversion and biological applications. Organic small molecules are relatively overlooked in photothermal conversion research. Inorganic photothermal materials often contain precious, nondegradable metals with potential safety issues. Two-dimensional frameworks and conjugated polymers suffer from poor synthesis reproducibility. Traditional organic dyes limit large-scale application due to cumbersome synthesis and poor photothermal stability. Stable neutral radicals are the basis for radical chemistry theory and multifunctional applications. Photothermal materials based on stable radicals can convert near-infrared light into heat via nonradiative decay.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether stable, air-stable open-shell radical materials can serve as efficient organic photothermal materials. The authors hypothesize that aromatic nitric acid radicals without steric hindrance protecting groups can be readily prepared and purified. They predict these neutral conjugated nitrogen oxide radicals will exhibit high thermal, electrochemical and light stability. The hypothesis is that high spin concentration will lead to highly nonradiative decay and enhanced photothermal conversion efficiency. They predict that strong donor-acceptor conjugation will reduce the optical bandgap and determine paramagnetic properties. The predicted outcome is that TPA-TPA-O6 will show the highest photothermal conversion performance and excellent photo-stability.

Methodological Details
The study synthesized four star-shaped aromatic nitric acid radical materials. The compounds are TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8. Different cores were introduced: triphenylamine, triazine, pyrene, and spiro fluorene. Materials were prepared via facile demethylation and consequent oxidation of phenolic hydroxyl precursors in air. The synthesis used low-cost starting materials and a simple two-step process with high yield. Radical species and physical properties were studied by cyclic voltammetry (CV). UV-vis-NIR spectroscopy was used to characterize optical absorption. Electron spin resonance (ESR) was used to characterize radical spin signal and concentration. Photoluminescence and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) tests were performed. CV curves were measured 15 cycles in dichloromethane with 0.1 M nBu4NPF6 as supporting electrolyte. The scan rate for CV measurements was 0.1 V/s. Precursors were dissolved in dichloromethane at a concentration of 5 mg/mL.

Procedures And Architectures
The methoxy substituted precursors were coated on carbon-glass electrode to form film during measurements. Potential values were reported with saturated calomel electrode as reference using Fc+/Fc couple (0.27 V) as internal standard. HOMO and LUMO energy levels were calculated based on the CV curves. The HOMO energy levels of the demethylated radicaloids were recorded as -4.90, -4.81, -4.97, and -4.84 eV. ESR was applied to characterize radical spin signal and concentration of the star-shaped molecules. The ESR test used a sample amount of 0.02 mmol. Photothermal properties were evaluated by monitoring temperature increment under irradiation via IR thermal camera. Star-shaped radical materials were irradiated by an 808 nm laser with power of 0.8 W cm^-2. An interfacial evaporation system used commercially available white polyurethane (PU) porous foam as support. TPA-TPA-O6 was loaded into PU foam by impregnating pure PU foam in solution and drying under 80 °C. The foam used had a 2.0 cm diameter with 30 mg of TPA-TPA-O6 loading.

Key Results
TPA-TPA-O6 film absorption showed a typical and great red shift compared with TPA-TPA-OMe. TPA-TPA-O6 radical powder is totally black, indicating wide absorption over the visible region. TPA-PY-O8 and TPA-TPZ-O6 exhibited obvious absorption with edges around 1000 nm and 800 nm in film. All demethylated counterparts exhibited highly reversible CV curves with negligible change after 15 cycles. The star-shaped ANARs exhibited unexpected electrochemical stability compared to traditional organic radical materials. The demethylated radicaloids showed comparable electrochemical and air stability with their methoxy precursors. The PLQYs of the radical products were all lower than 1%, indicating radical formation. The PLQYs of TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8 were recorded as 0.1%, 0.9%, 1.0%, and 0.3%. TPA-TPA-O6 and Spiro-O8 showed significantly enhanced ESR signal intensity due to more obvious radical character. TPA-TPA-O6 temperature increased rapidly from 25 °C to about 210 °C within 60 s under 0.8 W cm^-2. At 1.0 W cm^-2, the temperature of TPA-TPA-O6 raised up to about 250 °C within 60 s. TPA-TPA-O6 exhibited excellent stability for ten cycles of laser irradiation on and off.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The high spin concentration leads to highly nonradiative decay and enhanced photothermal conversion efficiency. The almost negligible radiation decay of TPA-TPA-O6 indicates great application potential in photothermal conversion. Aggregation in powder state extended the absorption of TPA-TPA-O6 from 300 to 2000 nm, facilitating sunlight harvesting. TPA-TPA-O6 exhibits extremely wide absorption spectra compared with other types of organic photothermal materials. The radical-promoted nonradiative decay mechanism explains the promising photothermal conversion performance. The equilibrium temperature of PU+TPA-TPA-O6 foam reached as high as 81.2 °C under 600 s continuous irradiation. The surface temperature of PU+TPA-TPA-O6 foam is remarkably higher than PU foam under 1 sun irradiation. The equilibrium temperature of the foam is 45 °C after 1 sun illumination for 1 h, about 10 °C higher than PU foam. The evaporation rate of 1.293 kg m^-2 h^-1 and efficiency of 89.41% represent top performance among pure organic small molecule photothermal materials. The pure organic radical compounds are extremely soluble in green solvents such as ethanol and DMSO. The stable open-shell radicals showed excellent solar-driven desalination performance with reduced primary ion concentrations.

Claims
Aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs) are stable, air-stable open-shell radicals suitable for photothermal conversion. ANARs exhibit high thermal, electrochemical and light stability. The star-shaped ANARs exhibited unexpected electrochemical stability. The compounds were prepared without steric hindrance protecting groups. The paper reports high stability, but does not compare with specific stability benchmarks. The design concept provides a novel strategy for stable high-spin radical materials.
